la:adv:olim.gloss: formerly, in time past, some time ago
senses: formerly, in time past, some time ago
one day, once, at some (future) time
la:adv:olim.html:
ōlim, adv.
ole, olle, ollus or olus, archaic for ille, with locative ending -im, = illo tempore, v. Brix ad
, lit.,
at that (sc. remote) time; hence,
Of past time, some time ago, once upon a time, once, formerly, in time past, whilom, erst (freq. and class.; syn. quondam): versibu' quos olim Fauni vatesque canebant, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 222 Vahl.): ut fuit olim Sisyphus,: sic enim olim loquebantur,: olim, vel nuper,; so corresp. to hoc tempore,: olim...mox,: ut erant olim,; cf.: alium esse censes nunc me, atque olim,; : gens olim armis, mox memoriā nominis clara,: fuit olim senex: ei filiae Duae erant,there was once an old man,.—
Transf.
From the meaning in times past is derived that of since ever (Germ. von jener), what used to happen, was, is, the old custom; hence, in propositions which state, as the result cf experience, that any thing is wont to take place, at times (only ante-class. and poet.): nunc lenonum plus est fere, Quam olim muscarum'st, cum caletur maxime,; cf. id. Mil. 1, 1, 2; ; cf. also : saxum tumidis submersum tunditur olim Fluctibus, etc.,; : ut pueris olim dant crustula blandi Doctores, Orell.: ut calceus olim, Si pede major erit, subvertet, si minor, uret,; : parentis olim si quis impiā manu Senile guttur fregerit,: ut olim Amisso dubiae rege vagantur apes,: color oris erat, qui frondibus olim Esse solet seris,; : an quid est olim homini salute melius?ever,: vestra meos olim si fistula dicat amores,if ever,.—
Now for a long time, this good while, long ago (mostly post-Aug.; not in Cic.): olim non librum in manus sumpsi: olim nescio, quid sit otium,: audio quid veteres olim moneatis amici,: nullas mihi epistulas mittas,: provisum erat,: corruptis moribus,: olim jam nec perit quicquam mihi nec acquiritur,.—
Of the future, one day, on a future day, at a future time, hereafter (rare but class.): audire edepol lubet. St. Primum omnium olim terra quom proscinditur, : utinam coram tecum olim, potius quam per epistulas!: exoriare aliquis ultor...Nunc, olim, quocumque dabunt se tempore vires,; cf.: non si male nunc et olim Sic erit,: forsan et haec olim meminisse juvabit,: numquid ego illi Imprudens olim faciam simile?: vir nominabitur,.

la:noun:oleum.html:
ŏlĕum, i, n., = ἔλαιον,
oil, olive-oil.
Lit., ; ; ; ; Lex. Thor. lin. 95 Rudorff. p. 191: instillare oleum lumini,: juventus Nudatos umeros oleo perfusa nitescit,; : ungere caules oleo meliore,; : BALNEVM CVM OLEO GRATVITO DEDIT,. —As a fig. of softness, gentleness: oleo tranquillior,quieter, gentler, stiller than oil,.—Prov.: oleum et operam perdere (alluding to nocturnal labors),to lose one's time and trouble, to spend them in vain,; : ne et opera et oleum philologiae nostrae perierit,; cf.: ante lucem cum scriberem contra Epicureos, de eodem oleo et operā exaravi nescio quid ad te,: petit hic (labor) plus temporis atque olei plus,: oleum addere camino, to add oil to the fire, i. e. to aggravate an evil, (cf. the Gr. πίττῃ καὶ ἐλαίῳ πῦρ κατασβεννύναι).—
Trop.
The palœstra (from the use of oil to anoint the bodies of wrestlers): ego eram decus olei,.—
Transf., literary contests or rhetorical exercises: genus verborum nitidum, sed palaestrae magis et olei, quam hujus civilis turbae ac fori,more proper for exercises in the school or for disputations, than for use in public,.—
(In eccl. Lat.) The spirit, inspiration: unxit te Deus oleo exultationis,; .

la:verb:oleo.gloss: to smell; to emit an odor, especially a bad odor
senses: to smell; to emit an odor, especially a bad odor
to be given away by smell; to smell of
la:verb:oleo.html:
ŏlĕo, lŭi, 2 (collat. form ŏlo, ĕre;
pres. subj. olat, Afran. ap. : olant,; . 3, 121; Pompon. ap. ). v. n. and a. [root od-; cf. Gr. ὄζω; v. odor], to smell (class.; cf. odoro, fragro).
To emit a smell, to smell of any thing.
Lit., constr. absol. or with acc., less freq. with abl. of that of which any thing smells: quid (jura) olant, nescias, nisi id unum, male ut olere intellegas,; : rosa recens a longinquo

olet, sicca propius, : olent, salsa sunt, ut tangere non velis,: mulieres ideo bene olere, quia nihil olebant, videbantur,; cf. : hesperis noctu magis olet,: ceram crocum olere,of wax,: olet unguenta,: unguenta exotica,: vina fere dulces oluerunt mane Camenae,.— With abl.: cur nardo flammae non oluere meae?: Arabo rore,: sulphure,.—In a bad sense: cui os oleat,i. e. who has a foul breath,; cf. .—

Trop., to smell of, savor of any thing; to indicate, betray any thing: quid igitur? quid olet? responde! Pen. Furtum, scortum, prandium, : nihil olere peregrinum,to savor of, betray,: nihil ex Academiā,: malitiam,: verba alumnum olent,betray,.—
To betray itself or be observed by its smell: aurum huic olet,i. e. he smells out, observes that I have money,: non olet, unde sit, quod dicitur cum illis?don't you perceive whence it comes?.—Hence, ŏlens, entis, P. a., smelling, odorous (mostly poet.).
Sweet-smelling, fragrant, odoriferous: rami olentes,: serpylla,: olentia pascua,: mentae,: Hymettus,.—
Lit., Stinking, foul, rank: leno,: maritus (i. e. hircus),: immundus olentia sudor Membra sequebatur,: Medi ora,: fornix,: stagna Palici, i. e. olentia sulphure,: agri (from dead bodies),.—
Trop.: quaedam,musty,

ŏlĕa, ae (
dat. plur. oleabus, Gell. ap. ), = ἐλαία.
Lit., an olive, olive-berry: olea ab elaea, Müll.: oleas caducas, et albas condire,: oleam cogere, legere, stringere, verberare,; cf. ; —
Transf., an olive-tree, : agricola cum florem oleae videt, bacam quoque se visurum putat. ; so ; ; ; : ure maris oleas,; ; .

la:noun:olla.html:
olla, ae (old form aula:
aulas antiqui dicebant, quas nos dicimus ollas, quia nullam litteram geminabant. Itaque aulicocia exta, quae in ollis coquebantur, dicebant, id est elixa, Müll.—Examples with aula, for olla, are found in ; ; sq.; ; ; ; 47; 4, 2, 4; 7; ; et saep.; ; ; sqq.; cf. also ), f.
root uk-, Sanscr. ukha, pot; aula for aukula
, a pot or jar: quadrilibrem aulam onustam auro habeo,; Varr. ap. : ollam denariorum implere,: fictilis,: monendus qui vasa emturus est, ne bibulas aut male coctas emat,: ET OLLAS PRECATI SVNT, Inscr. Fratr. Arv. tab. 41 a; cf. Marini Atti, p. 593: grandes fumabant pultibus ollae,.—For preserving the ashes of the dead, ; cf. ; Jahn, Specim. Epigr. p. 29 sq.—Prov.: olla male fervet, the pot boils poorly, i. e. the affair looks bad, : ipsa holera olla legit, the pot culls its own herbs, i. e. serves itself, : vultus redigentur in ollam,made as black as a pot,.—
Trop.: olla cujus rubigo in eā est,i. e. the city full of the vile,.

la:noun:Olympus.html:
Ŏlympus and -pos (anciently written Olĭmpus), i, m., = Ὄλυμπος.
The name of several mountains, the most celebrated of which is one on the borders of Macedonia and Thessaly (now Lacha), of great height, and consequently regarded as the seat of the gods, ; : Musae quae pedibus magnum pulsatis Olimpum, Enn. ap. Müll.: his diis Helicona atque Olympon attribuerunt homines,: frondosus,: opacus,: nubes excedit Olympus,.—
Transf., poet. for heaven: caelum dicunt Graeci Olympum,; : longus Olympus,the distant heavens,: annuit (Juppiter) et totum nutu tremefecit Olympum,: stelliger,.—Hence, ŏlympĭădes, um, f., the Muses (perh. only acc. to the foll. remark): caelum dicunt Graeci Olympum montem in Macedoniā omnes, a quo potius puto Musas dictas Olympiadas,.—

la:noun:oliva.html:
ŏlīva, ae, f.
ἐλαία
.
An olive, ; ; ; ; Afran. ap. : lecta de pinguissimis Oliva ramis arborum,: olea duarum vel trium olivarum in summitate rami,.—
Lit., an olive-tree: Aristaeus, qui olivae inventor dicitur,; : erum an bacis opulentet olivae,: numquam fallens,: clivus Olivarum,the Mount of Olives,: mons Olivarum,.—
Transf. (poet.).
An olive-branch: undique decerptam fronti praeponere olivam,.—
A staff of olive-wood, an olive-staff, .

la:noun:olivum.html:
ŏlīvum or ŏlīvom, i, n.
id.

Lit.
Oil (poet. and in post-class. prose for oleum): eme die caecā hercle olivum, id vendito oculatā die,; ; ; ; : inolens,: pingue,; : perfundere pisces olivo,: si ex olivis meis olivum feceris,.—
Trop., the palœstra (from the use of oil to anoint wrestlers): cur olivum vitat?; cf. oleum.—
Transf., an ointment, unguent: Syrio fragrans olivo,. 8; .

la:verb:olfacio.html:
olfăcĭo, ēci, actum, 3 (uncontracted collat. form ŏlĕfăcĭo:
olefacit, olefecit, olefactum,), v. a.
oleo-facio
, to smell, scent something (class.; syn. odoror).
Lit.: ea, quae gustemus, olfaciamus, tractemus, audiamus,: unguentum,: laurus folia trita olfactaque,smelled,: gith tusum, olfactum, (olefactum, Jahn).—Absol.: delphini sagacissime olfaciunt,have a very keen scent,.—
Trop., to smell, scent, surmise, detect any thing: non sex totis mensibus olfecissem, quam, etc.,: nummum,: nomen poëtae,.—*
To cause to smell of any thing: si ad matris mammam (agnus) non accedet, admovere oportet et olfacere labra lacte,.
